transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. I, um... I hope I'm in the right place for this. I've just been having a little trouble lately with... well, with my eating habits. 

I know it probably sounds silly, and I'm a little ashamed to even admit it, but... what really scares me is that sometimes, once I start eating—especially when I’m just alone in the kitchen—it feels almost like I’ve... stepped aside? Like I can’t make myself stop, even though I’m telling myself the whole time, you know, ‘Janet, put it away.’ But I just can't seem to do it. 

I'm sorry, does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay...
Can you tell me more about these times when you feel like you can't stop eating—how often does that happen, and what kinds of things are you eating when it occurs?

Well, it's really not every day, I promise. Usually, it's just... um, on some afternoons. Like, I volunteer a lot, so maybe after a shift at the food bank, or if I’ve been baking for a senior-center event... I’ll come home and, well, I'll start with just a full plate of leftovers. Which I think is normal, right? 

But then... I don't know, I just keep going. I might have a few slices of banana bread, and then some chips, and... some cheese, and then whatever cookies are left in the tin. 

It doesn't sound like that much when I try to justify it to myself, but afterward, when I really look at what I just did, I realize it was... well, it's way more than any meal I would ever serve to another person. I'm so sorry, I know I shouldn't let myself get carried away like that. Is... is that the kind of information you needed? I hope I'm answering your questions okay.
After these episodes of eating more than you intended, do you ever try to compensate for it by doing something like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

Oh, goodness, no. No, I would never do anything like that. I know some people struggle with those kinds of things, but... no, I don't make myself sick or take any pills like that. 

I mean, I try to be good the next day, you know? Maybe just have a salad for lunch or go for a nice walk around the neighborhood. Just normal things to try and balance it out a little bit. I always try to take care of my health, I really do. 

I hope that's the right answer... I mean, I hope it's okay that I don't do those things. Does that make sense?
During these episodes, do you feel like you're losing control over how much you're eating, even though you know you should stop?

Yes, exactly. Um, I think that's what I was trying to explain when we first sat down... it's just so embarrassing to admit. 

But yes, that's exactly what it feels like. Like I was saying earlier, when I'm alone in the kitchen, it’s almost like I’ve just... stepped aside from my own body. I know I should stop, and I'm literally telling myself in my head, 'Janet, just put it away, you don't need this.' But I just... I can't seem to make my hands stop reaching for things. 

I feel so silly even saying it out loud, because I know a grown woman should have more willpower than that. I really am trying my best to get a handle on it, I promise. Is that... is that the kind of feeling you were asking about? I hope I'm not repeating myself too much.
Do these episodes of eating more than you intend usually happen when you're feeling stressed, upset, or dealing with a low mood?

Um, well... I wouldn't say it's because I'm upset, really. I mean, everyone has a little stress, right? That's just life. But I try to stay very positive. I don't really get... depressed or anything like that. 

I guess sometimes if I've had a busy day helping out, or if I'm just feeling a little worn down, it might happen then. But it's not like I'm sitting there crying into a bowl of ice cream, I promise. I try to keep a very cheerful home. 

I just... I'm not entirely sure what triggers it, to be honest. I hope that's an okay answer? I know you're trying to find a pattern, and I'm sorry if I'm not being very helpful with that part. I just don't think it's because I'm sad. Does that make sense?
Do you ever find yourself eating even when you’re not really hungry, or continuing to eat even after you feel full?

Um, well... yes, I suppose that does happen sometimes. I mean, not all the time, of course! But... well, a lot of times, this happens after I've already had a perfectly nice supper. My husband and I eat a good meal, and my stomach isn't really asking for anything else, you know? 

But then... I don't know, I just find myself going back to the pantry or the fridge. Just to tidy up, usually, or to check on things for the next day. And I might just pick at a little something here or there... and then it sort of turns into a lot more than I meant to have. Even when I'm already quite full from dinner. 

It's such a silly habit, isn't it? I know I shouldn't be eating when I'm not hungry. I really am trying to be better about just closing the kitchen after supper. Am I explaining that right? I hope that gives you the information you need... I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly.
Do you ever find yourself eating in secret or feeling disgusted, ashamed, or guilty after these episodes of eating more than you intended?

Um... well... I guess I do try to make sure I'm alone when it happens. I don't really want anyone to see me, you know? It's not that I'm trying to be sneaky, I just... I don't want to bother my husband with it. 

But yes, afterward... oh, it's just dreadful. I feel so awful about myself. I look at the wrappers or the empty containers and I just think about how I've wasted food that I really meant to share with my family, or save for the next day. And I just sit there feeling so ashamed. I keep telling myself that I'm forty-eight years old, I'm a grown woman, I shouldn't be acting this way over food. 

I always promise myself it won't happen again. I really do mean it when I say it, too. I just... I hope you don't think terribly of me for admitting that. It's just so embarrassing. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Can you tell me if these episodes of eating more than you intend happen all in one sitting, and if so, about how long do they usually last?

Um, well... yes, I suppose it does all happen at once. Like, in one sitting. I mean, it doesn't take very long. Maybe an hour or so? 

Like, sometimes, on an afternoon after I've had a shift at the food bank, or maybe I've been baking for a senior-center event... I try to stay so busy and helpful, you know? But I'll come home and... well, I might start with a full plate of leftovers from the fridge. And then, I don't know, I just keep going. I'll have a few slices of banana bread, and then maybe some chips, some cheese... and whatever cookies are left in the tin. 

And then, when I finally stop, I look at everything and I realize... oh goodness, it was way more than I would ever serve to another person for a meal. It's just... it happens so fast, and I don't really mean to eat all of that. 

I know it sounds terrible when I say it out loud. I really am trying to be better about it. Does that answer your question about how long it takes? I hope I'm explaining it clearly enough... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right details.
During these episodes, do you feel like you're not in control of your eating, even though you're aware you should stop?

Um... well... yes. I suppose that's exactly what it feels like. I mean, I know I shouldn't be eating all of that, and I'm very aware of it while it's happening. 

It's just... oh, this is so hard to admit, but what really scares me is that once I start eating, especially when I'm alone in the kitchen like I mentioned before... it almost feels like I've just stepped aside, if that makes sense? Like I'm watching myself do it, and I can't seem to make myself stop. 

The whole time, I'm telling myself, "Janet, put it away. Just close the box." But my hands just keep moving. It's not that I want to be out of control, I really don't! I try very hard to keep things orderly. It's just... in those moments, it feels like I can't quite catch hold of the brakes. 

I know that must sound so weak. I really am trying to be stronger about it, I promise. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it in a way that's helpful for you... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what happens.
Can you tell me if, during these episodes, you feel like you're eating a much larger amount of food than most people would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances?

Um... yes. I suppose I sort of touched on that a moment ago, and I hope it's alright if I repeat myself a little, I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need. But yes... it's definitely more than most people would eat. 

Like I was saying about those afternoons when I come home from my shift at the food bank or from baking for the senior center... when I actually stop and look at what I've had, with the full plate of leftovers, and then the slices of banana bread, the chips, the cheese, and the cookies... well, it's quite a lot. I realize afterward that it's way, way more than any meal I would ever serve to another person. I would never expect a guest or my husband to eat all of that in just an hour. 

I feel so foolish admitting the actual amount, because I really do try to be sensible and healthy most of the time. But during those specific episodes... yes, it's a much larger amount than normal. Does that answer your question properly? I just want to be sure I'm doing this right and giving you the information you need.
During these episodes, do you feel completely unable to control how much you eat, like you're powerless to stop yourself even though you want to?

Um... yes, I think we did sort of touch on this just a moment ago. I hope you don't mind me repeating myself, I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you're asking. 

But yes, it really is like I'm completely powerless to stop. Like I said before, it's... well, it's what scares me the most about the whole thing. When I'm alone in the kitchen and I start, it really does feel like I've just stepped aside. I'm standing there, and my brain is saying, "Janet, put it away, just close the box," but my hands just won't listen. 

I really don't want to be out of control. I try so hard to keep everything nice and orderly in my life. But in those moments, I just... I can't seem to stop myself, no matter how much I want to. 

I know I've said that already, and I really hope I'm not being repetitive or wasting your time. Does that help clarify things? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so you can understand what's happening.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient experiences a lack of control over eating during episodes, which is key to differentiating between F50.2 (Binge Eating Disorder), F50.8 (Other Specified Feeding or Eating Disorder), and F50.9 (Unspecified Feeding or Eating Disorder).
doctor.question: During these episodes, do you feel completely unable to control how much you eat, like you're powerless to stop yourself even though you want to?

patient.answer:
Um... yes, I think we did sort of touch on this just a moment ago. I hope you don't mind me repeating myself, I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you're asking. 

But yes, it really is like I'm completely powerless to stop. Like I said before, it's... well, it's what scares me the most about the whole thing.
